original.verbatim: The legality of the abortion medication mifepristone in the US has become uncertain due to conflicting court rulings. Texas US District Judge Matthew Kacsmaryk ordered a hold on federal approval of mifepristone, overruling decades of scientific approval. This ruling occurred at nearly the same time US District Judge Thomas O. Rice ordered US authorities not to restrict access to the drug in 17 states. The conflicting decisions may lead to an accelerated path for the issue to reach the Supreme Court. Mifepristone has been widely used in the US since receiving FDA approval and has no precedent for a single judge overruling the FDA's medical decisions. Mifepristone is one of two drugs used for medication abortion, and complications from the drug occur at a lower rate than many routine medical procedures. If mifepristone is pulled from the market, clinics may switch to using only the second drug, misoprostol, which has a slightly lower effectiveness in ending pregnancies.
